subject: maths
question: P and Q can complete a project in 15 days and 10 days, respectively. They started doing the work together, but after 2 days, Q had to leave and P alone completed the remaining work. In how many days was the whole work completed?
solution:
(P + Q)'s 1 day's work = 1/15 + 1/10

⇒ (2 + 3)/30

⇒ 5/30

⇒ 1/6 

Work done by P and Q in 2 days = 1/6 × 2

⇒ 1/3

Remaining work = 1 - 1/3

⇒ 2/3

Now,

1/15 work is done by P in 1 day.

So, 2/3 work will be done by P in 15 × 2/3 = 10 days

So, the total time is taken = 10 + 2

⇒ 12 days

**∴ The whole work was completed in 12 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Calculation: 

LCM of 15, 10 is 30

Efficiency of P = 30/15 = 2

Efficiency of Q = 30/10 = 3

Two days of work will be (2 + 3) × 2 = 10

Remaining work = 30 - 10 = 20

As Q left remaining work will be done by P = 20/2 = 10 days

**Total work done in 10 + 2 = 12 days**
